monthly_review.summary: You've increased training volume and intensity this month, with faster average pace and higher aerobic training effect, but at the cost of reduced cadence and slightly elevated HR — suggesting a shift toward more demanding efforts.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite 4 fewer runs and 9.4 km less total distance than last month, your average pace improved by 20 sec/km and aerobic TE rose by 0.3 — indicating higher-intensity efforts per run.

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.4 more km across 4 sessions in the remaining 13 days to match last month’s volume — averaging 2.35 km per session, or alternatively 2x 3.5 km + 2x 1.2 km runs.

insights.title: Efficiency gains despite pace increase
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved from 13.46 to 13.52 while average pace quickened — suggesting better metabolic economy at faster efforts, likely supported by your recent long run (14.1 km at 9:23 min/km) and consistent Zone 3–4 work (46% of HR time).

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity distribution
insights.body: Zone 4+ time increased from 16% (15% Z4 + 1% Z5) last month to 26% (19% Z4 + 7% Z5) this month — particularly evident in your 12.0 km (9:15 min/km, 144 bpm) and 14.1 km (9:23 min/km, 141 bpm) runs — signaling greater reliance on threshold and VO2 max efforts.

insights.title: Cadence drop correlates with longer, slower efforts
insights.body: Avg cadence fell from 151 to 147 spm, and your two longest runs (14.1 km and 12.0 km) showed cadences of 151 and 153 spm respectively — but stride length dropped sharply (70.4 cm vs. 86.4 cm in shorter runs), suggesting fatigue-induced form compromise late in long efforts.

insights.title: Minimal true recovery running
insights.body: Only 14% of this month’s time was spent in Zone 1 (vs. 24% last month), and your shortest run was just 0.9 km — no true easy/recovery sessions (<120 bpm, <6:30 min/km) appear in recent logs, increasing cumulative fatigue risk.

recommendations.action: Do one 5.0 km run at Zone 2 HR ≤135 bpm and pace ≤8:45 min/km (≤525 sec/km) before July 25th
recommendations.reason: Your lowest recent HR was 129 bpm (4.0 km run), but Zone 2 is underutilized — this will restore recovery capacity and support aerobic base amid rising intensity.

recommendations.action: Add 2x 4-minute Zone 4 intervals (HR ≥158 bpm, pace ~4:35–4:45 min/km) with 3-min Zone 1/2 jog recovery, embedded in an 8 km total run
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 4 time is up 4% MoM but lacks structured interval stimulus — this leverages your current VO2 max (39–40) and improves lactate buffering without overloading weekly volume.

recommendations.action: Perform a 10-minute post-run mobility routine focusing on hip flexors and calves after every run >5 km
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time increased to 314–319 ms in long runs (vs. 300–301 ms in short runs), indicating stiffness or fatigue — mobility can help preserve stride integrity and reduce vertical oscillation drift.

weekly_focus.description: Rebalance training stress by integrating one true recovery run, one structured threshold session, and one endurance-focused long run — all while protecting form and HR discipline.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 Recovery Run (5 km, HR ≤135 bpm)
Threshold Intervals (2x 4-min Z4 w/3-min Z1–2 recovery)
Long Run (10–12 km, avg HR 138–142 bpm, cadence ≥148 spm)
